record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.original_question: For matrix norms that satisfy submultiplicativity or mixed submultiplicativity, determine whether such norms must be induced norms or whether some of them cannot be induced. The source explicitly asks for a structural characterization of inducedness within these broader multiplicative classes.

evidence.quote: More generally, it is possible to define matrix norms that satisfy submultiplicativity ... or mixed submultiplicativity ... conditions [37-39].
Is it possible to show that such norms are induced or cannot be induced?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}$ and, for each pair $(m,n)$ of positive integers, let $\|\cdot\|_{m,n}$ be a norm on the space $\mathbb{F}^{m	imes n}$ of $m	imes n$ matrices. The family $\{\|\cdot\|_{m,n}\}$ is called:

(a) submultiplicative if for all positive integers $m,p,n$ and all $A\in\mathbb{F}^{m	imes p}$, $B\in\mathbb{F}^{p	imes n}$,
$$\|AB\|_{m,n}\le \|A\|_{m,p}\,\|B\|_{p,n};$$

(b) mixed submultiplicative if there exist norms $\|\cdot\|_{m,n}$, $\|\cdot\|'_{m,p}$, $\|\cdot\|''_{p,n}$ (possibly distinct) such that for all compatible $A,B$,
$$\|AB\|_{m,n}\le \|A\|'_{m,p}\,\|B\|''_{p,n}.$$

A family of matrix norms $\{\|\cdot\|_{m,n}\}$ is called induced (operator) if there exist vector norms $
u_k$ on $\mathbb{F}^k$ for every $k\ge 1$ such that
$$\|A\|_{m,n}=\sup_{x\in\mathbb{F}^n\setminus\{0\}} rac{
u_m(Ax)}{
u_n(x)}$$
for every $A\in\mathbb{F}^{m	imes n}$.

Give a structural characterization that determines, for an arbitrary submultiplicative (resp. mixed submultiplicative) family of matrix norms, whether the family must be an induced family or whether it cannot be realized as an induced family. Equivalently, provide necessary and sufficient conditions on the family $\{\|\cdot\|_{m,n}\}$ for the existence (or nonexistence) of vector norms $\{
u_k\}$ realizing it as an operator norm.
artifact.status_search_result: It is well known that every induced matrix norm is submultiplicative and that the Frobenius norm is a submultiplicative but non-induced norm, so individual instances of non-inducedness are classical. However, a general structural characterization that decides inducedness within the broader classes of (mixed) submultiplicative matrix norm families does not appear to be settled in the literature surveyed. Status is therefore best described as unknown/open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: Matrix norm - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Although the Frobenius norm is not an induced matrix norm, it still has the submultiplicative property.
status_evidence.claim: There exist concrete submultiplicative matrix norms (e.g. Frobenius) that are not induced norms, but a general characterization of inducedness within submultiplicative families is not stated.

status_evidence.title: ALAFF Submultiplicative norms
status_evidence.snippet: A consistent matrix norm is said to be submultiplicative if ||AB|| ≤ ||A|| ||B||; induced norms are submultiplicative but not every submultiplicative norm is induced.
status_evidence.claim: Standard treatments confirm the strict inclusion of induced norms within submultiplicative norms but do not give a general structural characterization.
